rfm_tuples.R: 'One customer, Shanghai Lansheng, our China distributor who sells into China and Hong Kong, accounted for approximately 58% of our consolidated net sales during fiscal 2023.' Three-year ramp: 2021 46.6% -> 2022 52.1% -> 2023 57.6%. (Item 1 + Risk Factors)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A - Verify the concentration percentage against segment table (China region disclosure) in same 10-K. Mode B - derive: if China dependence is rising and the underlying China economy is decelerating (acknowledged in Risk Factors), the consolidated business is functionally a long position on one Chinese distributor's willingness to keep absorbing inventory.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1 + Item 1A + Note: Segment / Geographic disclosure (China sales $185.6M / total $322.4M = 57.6%)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Concentration is rising 11 pp in 2 years to 58%. The 10-K itself flags 'China accounted for approximately 58% of our fiscal 2023 consolidated net sales' as a top risk factor. Q1 2024 10-Q (filed 2024-05-07) reports China distributors at 49% of Q1 net sales vs 48% Q1 2023 (consistent quarter but down from FY23 58% blended) and China sales grew only +10% YoY in Q1 vs +25% China growth in FY2023 vs +38% in FY2022 - sharp deceleration on the single dominant customer.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Single-customer / single-country dependence at 58% is itself a structural red flag; the disclosure is honest but the trend (concentration rising while end-market growth decelerates) is the Mode-B catch. STAA is not a global medical-device company - it is a Shanghai Lansheng / China ICL volume bet with a US head office.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Accounts receivable, net was $94.7 million and $62.4 million at December 29, 2023 and December 30, 2022, respectively. Days' Sales Outstanding (DSO) was 113 and 89 days, respectively for 2023 and 2022. The increase in DSO in 2023 was temporary and was due to extended payment terms to our largest customer outside of the U.S. due to unfavorable foreign currency conditions. We have a solid and lengthy relationship with this customer, for which collectability is reasonably assured.' (MD&A)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A - Verify AR / DSO math against balance sheet. Mode B - derive: 'extended payment terms' for the dominant 58%-of-revenue customer in the same fiscal year that revenue posted +13% YoY ($322M vs $284M) is functionally a financing-side concession - the seller is funding the buyer. Verify whether Q1'24 10-Q shows AR normalizing or extension renewed.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K MD&A (AR $94.7M, DSO 113d); Q1'24 10-Q balance sheet (AR $64.6M at Mar 29, 2024); 10-K Statement of Cash Flows (AR change -$32.8M)
rfm_tuples.M_value: DSO jumped 24 days (+27%) in the year revenue grew 13%. The seller funded ~$32.8M of incremental receivables to keep China shipments flowing. Q1 2024 AR fell from $94.7M to $64.6M - i.e. STAAR collected ~$30M from Shanghai Lansheng in Q1, confirming the FY23 stretch was a real cash collection issue, not just timing. Management framing 'temporary' is post-hoc justified by Q1 collection but the use of seller-financing to grow into a single distributor that already takes 58% of sales is a working-capital quality red flag pattern.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: AR did normalize in Q1 which validates the 'temporary' framing, but only after a one-time 24-day DSO expansion that masked underlying demand softness in the China distributor's sell-through. The Mode-B finding is that 'collectability is reasonably assured' is a present-tense claim that does not address the next leg - if China end-demand stays at +10% growth (Q1) vs +25% (FY23), the distributor will not need / cannot afford the inventory absorption that drove FY23 sales.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Inventories, net was $35.1 million and $24.2 million at December 29, 2023 and December 30, 2022, respectively. Days' Inventory on Hand (DOH) was 142 and 94 days for 2023 and 2022, respectively, for finished goods, including consignment inventory. The increase in DOH was due to a planned increase of production to support sales growth of ICL products.' (MD&A)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A - Verify DOH math and inventory build vs sales. Mode B - derive: simultaneous +51% DOH AND +27% DSO is a textbook 'channel + own-warehouse' inventory accumulation pattern - both the seller and the distributor are holding more lenses than current sell-through justifies. Cross-check Q1'24 to see if DOH worsened.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K MD&A + Balance Sheet ($35.1M FY23 vs $24.2M FY22); Q1'24 10-Q ($38.6M at Mar 29, 2024); Cash flow statement (inventory build -$14.4M FY23)
rfm_tuples.M_value: DOH expanded 48 days (+51%) on revenue growth of only +13%. Q1 2024 inventory grew further to $38.6M (+10% sequential from $35.1M) on Q1 revenue +5.2% YoY. Inventory provisions jumped to $4.85M (FY23) from $2.42M (FY22) - the reserve doubled, confirming management itself sees obsolescence/expiry risk on the build. CRITICAL: STAAR built inventory AND simultaneously the distributor stretched payment terms - this is the bilateral fingerprint of either (a) a channel-stuffed FY23 sales number or (b) over-investment in capacity ahead of expected ICL volume that hasn't arrived. Either reading is unfavorable.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The DOH+DSO joint expansion is the single most diagnostic forensic signal in this filing. 'Planned increase of production to support sales growth' is the management-provided narrative; the Mode-B reframing is that production was planned in 2022 against a China demand assumption that the macro deterioration acknowledged in Item 1A has already invalidated. Inventory provision doubling is the auditor / management's own implicit acknowledgement. High forensic priority.

rfm_tuples.R: 'We have served as the Company's auditor since 1993.' (Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm, BDO USA, P.C., Los Angeles, PCAOB ID 243) + 'We identified the realization of the Company's deferred tax assets, including the judgment and estimation regarding projected taxable income as a critical audit matter.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A - Verify auditor identity, tenure, PCAOB ID, and CAM disclosure. Mode B - derive: BDO USA is tier-2 (not Big 4) for a healthcare-device company with $322M revenue and $185M China concentration. A Big 4 firm would typically be expected at this scale. Check for any auditor disagreements, dismissals, or NT filings.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K auditor report (BDO USA, P.C.; Los Angeles, California; PCAOB ID 243); EDGAR 8-K Item 4.01 search (none found in pre-cutoff period for STAA)
rfm_tuples.M_value: BDO USA - mid-tier auditor (not Big 4), 31-year continuous tenure (since 1993). No 8-K Item 4.01 (auditor change) in EDGAR pre-cutoff window. ICFR opinion is unqualified, no material weakness disclosed, SOX 302 certifications standard. Critical Audit Matter is deferred-tax realizability - i.e. the auditor's #1 worry is whether STAA will actually earn enough future taxable income to use its DTAs, which is itself a forward-looking concession that the auditor is uncertain about forecasted profitability. No going-concern language.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: BDO tenure of 31 years is long-term audit-relationship risk for a company with 58% single-customer China concentration - relationship inertia exists. But there is no smoking-gun auditor finding (no MW, no GC, no disagreements). The CAM on deferred tax realizability is a soft tell that the auditor itself is uncertain about projected profitability, which is consistent with the demand-deceleration thesis. Mid-grade signal.

rfm_tuples.R: 'with respect to our 2022 internal review of compliance with certain regulations in the Japanese market related to sales of pre-loaded aphakic intraocular lenses for use in cataract surgery (IOLs, not ICLs)' (Item 1A, FCPA risk factor)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A - Verify the 2022 Japan internal review reference; Mode B - derive: a one-off FCPA-adjacent internal review that surfaces ONCE in a risk factor and is parenthetically minimized ('IOLs, not ICLs') is the disclosure pattern of an issue that management does not want to draw attention to. Check whether the 10-K provides outcome / resolution detail or only the historical existence.
rfm_tuples.M_value: The 2022 Japan internal review is mentioned exactly once across the 10-K, in a generic FCPA risk-factor paragraph, with parenthetical scope-limiting language. No corresponding 8-K disclosure of the review's existence, outcome, remediation, or any government inquiry was found in the EDGAR record pre-cutoff. No discussion of magnitude, employees disciplined, controls remediated. The IOL product line is being phased out per Item 1 - so the disclosure can also be read as 'the problem business is the one we're exiting.'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B finding: management disclosed the bare existence of a 2022 internal FCPA-adjacent review without quantification, status, or remediation. The minimizing framing is engineered to satisfy disclosure obligations while not creating a headline. For a company with 58% China and material Japan exposure, the precedent of an internal compliance review on payments-to-customers is worth flagging - but no contemporaneous evidence of escalation.

rfm_tuples.R: 'we manufacture hundreds of different types of lenses. This requires us to carry a significant amount of inventory to meet customer preference for rapid delivery ... During fiscal 2023, we continued to increase our inventory levels to meet the significant level of anticipated demand for our ICL lenses.' (Item 1) + Q1 2024 revenue $77.4M vs $73.5M Q1'23 = +5.2% YoY (vs FY23 growth of +13% and 2022 growth of +23%)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A - Verify Q1 2024 revenue growth rate against FY23 / FY22 prior trajectory; Mode B - derive: if Q1 2024 growth has decelerated to +5% while the 10-K narrative was built around 'significant anticipated demand,' the inventory build of FY23 is at risk of becoming a margin-compressing overhang.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1 + Q1 2024 10-Q Statement of Operations (Net sales $77.356M vs $73.528M)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Revenue growth path: 2021 +27%, 2022 +23%, 2023 +13%, Q1 2024 +5.2%. Deceleration is monotone. China specifically: FY22 +38%, FY23 +25%, Q1 2024 +10%. Q1 2024 operating result swung to a $(2.3)M operating LOSS from a $2.8M operating profit Q1 2023. Q1 net loss $(3.3)M vs net income $2.7M Q1 2023. R&D up +30% YoY, G&A up +28% YoY against revenue +5% YoY. Management commentary in 10-K does not project deceleration - 'significant anticipated demand' framing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Claim evolution between 10-K (Feb 27 filing date, narrative of 'significant anticipated demand') and the Q1 10-Q (May 7, swung-to-loss with revenue +5%) is sharp. The 10-K narrative is incompatible with the Q1 print. Either Q1 is a temporary blip or the 10-K narrative was over-optimistic - the prior covenant (rising DSO, rising DOH, rising inventory provisions) supports the latter. This is the framework's classic Mode-B 'claim evolution between 10-K and prior 10-Q' (here, 10-K and SUBSEQUENT 10-Q) catch.

rfm_tuples.M_value: $224M cash at Q1 2024, no funded debt, generated $21.7M operating cash in Q1 2024 (vs $(5.1)M Q1 2023 - actually IMPROVED on cash conversion as Shanghai Lansheng paid down AR). rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is the critical caveat for the SHORT thesis: STAAR is NOT a balance-sheet distress story. It is a single-customer + single-country + decelerating-end-market + channel-inventory story. The drawdown to date is unlikely to be solvency-driven. A short position depends on multiple compression / earnings disappointment from continued demand deceleration, NOT on liquidity collapse.

rfm_tuples.R: 'During 2023, foreign currency exchange rates between the U.S. dollar and the Chinese yuan experienced volatility. As the U.S. dollar strengthened relative to the Chinese yuan, it became more expensive for our China distributor to purchase ICLs and to pay prior accounts receivable balances. Our China distributor, who sells into China and Hong Kong, accounted for approximately 58% of our consolidated net sales during fiscal 2023.' (MD&A)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A - Verify the FX explanation is internally consistent (USD-denominated sales to China per the 10-K). Mode B - derive: the disclosure links DSO expansion (C2), the AR build, and the China concentration into one cohesive narrative - that yuan weakness IS the working-capital channel through which China deceleration shows up first. If yuan stays weak post-cutoff, the FY23 dynamics will recur and worsen.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Sales to China are denominated in USD per explicit 10-K disclosure. USDCNY appreciation 2022->2023 was meaningful. The mechanism: yuan weakens -> distributor's RMB cost of USD-denominated ICLs rises -> sell-through pricing power weakens or distributor squeezes margin -> distributor stretches payables back to STAAR -> STAAR's DSO rises. This is a one-way FX channel because pricing is USD. If yuan continues to weaken, the same mechanism applies in FY2024.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest mechanistic disclosure of the FX-to-AR channel, but the Mode-B point is that this is a STRUCTURAL fragility, not a one-time event. The 10-K presents it as 'temporary'; the same language was implicit in prior filings about prior FX episodes. As long as China = 58% and pricing is USD, this risk re-arms every cycle of yuan weakness.

rfm_tuples.R: Phase-out of cataract IOL product line ('Historically, the Company also manufactured and sold intraocular lenses (or IOLs) for use in surgery to treat cataracts. As the Company has focused its business and strategy on its ICL product offerings, we have phased out our cataract IOL product line.') + ICL share rising from 92% (2021) to 95% (2022) to 99% (2023) of sales.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A - Verify product mix shift in segment reporting. Mode B - derive: as ICL share goes from 92% to 99%, the company's revenue stream becomes more concentrated on a single product family AND on the China end market simultaneously - dual concentration risk increasing.
rfm_tuples.M_value: ICL share of total sales: 92% (2021) -> 95% (2022) -> 99% (2023). Combined with China share (47%/52%/58%), the conditional probability that revenue is 'one product to one country' is rising: in 2023, ~57% of revenue is China-ICL (vs ~43% in 2021). Strategic narrative frames this as focus; quantitatively it is increased concentration on a refractive (elective) procedure that depends on Chinese consumer discretionary spending.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 'focus on ICL' strategic framing is technically accurate but the Mode-B reframing is that STAAR has voluntarily exited diversification (IOL cataract line) at the same time its concentration on a single elective-procedure end market in a single decelerating country has risen. The drawdown the stock has already taken is consistent with the market re-pricing this dual concentration.

summary: STAAR is NOT a balance-sheet distress story (no debt, $224M cash, no covenant amendments, no going-concern, no material weakness) but it IS a demand-quality / concentration / channel-inventory distress story. The dominant signals are: (i) bilateral DSO+DOH expansion (113d vs 89d AR; 142d vs 94d inventory) during FY23 that screams either channel-stuffing or over-production into decelerating demand, (ii) China end-market growth decelerated +38% -> +25% -> +10% (Q1'24) on the single customer that takes 58% of sales, (iii) 10-K 'significant anticipated demand' narrative contradicted by Q1'24 swing to operating loss eight weeks after the 10-K was filed. Counter-pulling: (a) director Weisner cash buy at $38.11 + 13D holder Broadwood cash buy at $42.56 + zero insider sales is a non-fraud insider pattern, (b) Q1'24 collected $30M of China AR confirming the 'temporary' framing on collectability, (c) BDO is mid-tier but no MW / disagreements. Verdict: framework is detecting MODERATE forensic distress without solvency risk. The drawdown to cutoff likely already prices in the de-rating; further downside requires continued China demand deterioration, which is the base case but not certain.
